applies_to_stage: S2 onward: one joint, two-joint layout options, four pitch legs and eventual lateral joints; not a prerequisite for S0/S1 fixed-track research
status: cost-constrained selection; no new pitch actuator approved for purchase
baseline_strategy: Maintain a cheap-to-expensive planning ladder: DIY BLDC/cycloidal, integrated brushless robot joint, and high-end Dynamixel. Retain reduced owned XL430 and brushed encoder gearmotor as additional budget comparators. Compare complete installed systems at the same load, speed and duty; the ranking is provisional until fit, power and full costs are established. Direct XL430 pitch failed the earlier load screen.
high_end_aspirational_reference: Larger Dynamixels remain an aspirational option. XM540-W270-T is the priced TTL example, not a near-term budget assumption or a qualified ultimate-joint selection.
ultimate_destination: Four powerful tracked legs with independent pitch and lateral movement. Assuming one lateral axis per leg, plan for eight positioning axes plus four track drives. Lateral axis orientation awaits clarification; pitch and lateral actuators need separate sizing.

Eight-axis totals only show scale using identical units; they do not select identical pitch/lateral actuators. Final bills must include every excluded item before choosing a route.

bldc_evidence.finding: Compact combined MCU and three-phase power board with current sensing; concrete alternative to assuming the gimbal Shield suits a drone motor
Manufacturer specifies gimbal use and warns that high-power drone motors can damage the driver; the proposed generic cheap pairing is not established

14-bit single-turn angle does not identify absolute arm position after reduction/restart. At 40:1 the same motor angle recurs every 9 degrees of arm rotation; output sensing or a valid reference procedure is required

Author reports 19:1, 454 g, diameter 80 x 67 mm and over 12 N m supported statically using ODrive; dynamic result lower. Feasibility example, not continuous rating, full-system cost or Skala fit evidence

selection_requirements: First establish whole-robot packaging and electrical feasibility. Reject or explicitly cost any required change to chassis/deck, track spacing, battery, stop circuitry, distribution, cooling or propulsion before describing a route as cheaper.
Compare complete installed cost for one corner and four corners, including inventory shortfall and custom fabrication; partial subtotals cannot choose a winner.
Use sustained torque at required speed, gearbox permissible torque, thermal duty and actual total mass; stall torque is not a continuous rating.

Track output angle across the whole transmission; incremental counting loses its reference on restart, and a single-turn absolute motor sensor does not identify the output turn after reduction or detect a failed coupling.
Place drivers, sensor targets, bearings, connectors and service access in CAD before replacement prints; R1 clearances do not transfer to another motor.

Qualify one corner before ordering or printing four sets. Include lifting and dwell duty, simultaneous electrical load, temperature, current, backlash/wear, restart referencing, lost communications, power-off behavior and full cable sweep. No stair or power-off holding rating is established.
